title: Saudi Arabia's Q1 2026 Budget Deficit Hits SAR 125.7B — Largest Since 2018; Vision 2030 Contracts Frozen
detail: Analysis published on May 22 detailed Saudi Arabia's Q1 2026 fiscal results: the Kingdom recorded a deficit of SAR 125.7 billion (~$33.5 billion), the largest single-quarter shortfall since 2018. Government expenditure rose 20% year-on-year to SAR 386.69 billion, driven by a 26% surge in military spending related to the Iran war and a near-tripling of consumer subsidies as fuel and food costs rose. Oil revenues fell sharply as actual crude production collapsed to 6.77 million bpd — well below the OPEC+ quota of 10.291 million bpd — due to the Hormuz closure. The Ministry of Finance halted new contracts with Western consultancies and delayed payments on existing contracts pending special ministerial pre-approval. Key Vision 2030 mega-projects including core NEOM components have been delayed or downsized. The full-year 2026 deficit is projected at approximately SAR 165 billion (3.3% of GDP), though the Q1 figure alone already far exceeds that annual pace. The IMF downgraded Saudi Arabia's 2026 growth forecast by 1.4 percentage points to 3.1%.

media.caption: Saudi Arabia posts record SAR 125.7B Q1 2026 deficit as Iran war drives military spending surge and oil revenue collapse

title: Saudi Arabia's Evolving Sports Strategy: Football and Esports Replace LIV Golf as PIF Pivots to 2034 World Cup
detail: Reporting from The National on May 22 outlined Saudi Arabia's revised sports investment strategy following PIF's decision to end LIV Golf funding after 2026. The new focus consolidates around three pillars: association football (anchored by the 2034 FIFA World Cup hosting bid won in 2024 and the Saudi Pro League's aggressive player acquisition), the Qiddiya entertainment mega-city near Riyadh (projected to host an e-sport arena, theme parks, and live events), and esports as a growth sector targeting Saudi Arabia's young, digitally connected population (median age 29). PIF's sports subsidiary SRJ Sports Investments will manage the transition. Analysts noted the strategic pivot reflects both budget pressure from the Iran war-driven fiscal deficit and lessons learned from LIV Golf's limited brand-building returns relative to cost. The 2034 World Cup, estimated to require $20 billion in stadium and infrastructure investment, remains Vision 2030's highest-profile remaining mega-event.

media.caption: Saudi Arabia pivots sports strategy post-LIV Golf: football, Qiddiya, and esports now core to Vision 2030 entertainment agenda
